nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a primitive recursive encoding into $\mathbb{N}$. If $p$ and $q$ are recursively enumerable predicates on $\alpha$, then the predicate $a \mapsto p(a) \land q(a)$ is recursively enumerable.
nodes.title: Recursively enumerable predicates are closed under conjunction

nodes.summary: Let $p$ and $q$ be predicates on a type $\alpha$ with a primitive recursive encoding. If $p$ and $q$ are both decidable by multi-stack machines, then so is the predicate $a \mapsto p(a) \wedge q(a)$.
nodes.title: Decidable predicates are closed under conjunction

nodes.summary: Let $p$ and $q$ be predicates on a type $\alpha$ with a primitive recursive encoding. If $p$ and $q$ are both recognizable by multi-stack machines, then so is the predicate $a \mapsto p(a) \wedge q(a)$.
nodes.title: Recognizable predicates are closed under conjunction

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a primitive recursive encoding into $\mathbb{N}$. If $p$ and $q$ are computable predicates on $\alpha$, then the predicate $a \mapsto p(a) \land q(a)$ is computable.
nodes.title: Computable predicates are closed under conjunction

nodes.summary: For a Boolean-valued function $f$ on words over an alphabet $\sigma$, the language of $f$ is the set of words $u$ over $\sigma$ with $f(u) = \mathrm{true}$.
nodes.title: Language of a Boolean test

nodes.summary: Let $\gamma$ and $\beta$ be types with primitive recursive encodings into $\mathbb{N}$, let $l$ be a computable function sending each $x \in \gamma$ to a finite list $l(x)$ of elements of $\beta$, and let $g$ be a computable Boolean-valued function of $x \in \gamma$ and $b \in \beta$. Then the Boolean-valued function that sends $x$ to true exactly when $g(x, b)$ is true for some $b$ in $l(x)$ is computable.
nodes.title: Searching a computable list with a computable test is computable

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $\sigma$ with a primitive recursive encoding. If membership in $L$ is decidable by a multi-stack machine, then there is a computable function $f$ from words over $\sigma$ to Booleans such that $L$ is the language of $f$, that is, the set of words $u$ with $f(u) = \mathrm{true}$.
nodes.title: Decidable languages have computable membership tests

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be types with primitive recursive encodings into $\mathbb{N}$, let $R$ be a relation between $\alpha$ and $\beta$ that is recursively enumerable as a predicate on pairs $(a, b)$, and let $c$ be a primitive recursive function sending each $a \in \alpha$ to a finite list $c(a)$ of elements of $\beta$. Then the predicate $a \mapsto \exists b \in c(a),\ R(a, b)$ is recursively enumerable.
nodes.title: Bounded existential quantification preserves recursive enumerability

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be types with primitive recursive encodings into $\mathbb{N}$, and let $R$ be a relation between $\alpha$ and $\beta$ that is recursively enumerable as a predicate on pairs $(a, b)$. Then there is a partial recursive function $g$ from $\alpha$ to $\beta$ such that, for every $a \in \alpha$, if $g(a)$ is defined then its value $b$ satisfies $R(a, b)$, and $g(a)$ is defined whenever some…
nodes.title: Selection for r.e. relations

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be types with primitive recursive encodings into $\mathbb{N}$, and let $R$ be a relation between $\alpha$ and $\beta$ that is recursively enumerable as a predicate on pairs $(a, b)$. Then the predicate $a \mapsto \exists b \in \beta,\ R(a, b)$ is recursively enumerable.
nodes.title: Existential projection preserves recursive enumerability

nodes.summary: Given a letter $a$ and a list $\pi = [u_1, \dots, u_k]$ of words, the extensions of $\pi$ by $a$ are listed as follows: first $[[a], u_1, \dots, u_k]$, which starts a new piece $[a]$, and then, only when $k \ge 1$, also $[a u_1, u_2, \dots, u_k]$, which puts the letter $a$ in front of the first piece.
nodes.title: Extending a list of pieces by a letter

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be types with primitive recursive encodings into $\mathbb{N}$, let $R$ be a relation between $\alpha$ and $\beta$ that is recursively enumerable as a predicate on pairs $(a, b)$, and let $c$ be a primitive recursive function sending each $a \in \alpha$ to a finite list $c(a)$ of elements of $\beta$. Then the predicate $a \mapsto \forall b \in c(a),\ R(a, b)$ is recursively enumerable.
nodes.title: Bounded universal quantification preserves recursive enumerability

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $\sigma$ with a primitive recursive encoding. If membership in $L$ is decidable by a multi-stack machine, then so is membership in the Kleene star $L^*$, the set of all concatenations $u_1 \cdots u_k$ with $k \ge 0$ and $u_1, \dots, u_k \in L$.
nodes.title: Decidable languages are closed under Kleene star

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $\sigma$ with a primitive recursive encoding. If membership in $L$ is recognizable by a multi-stack machine, then so is membership in the Kleene star $L^*$, the set of all concatenations $u_1 \cdots u_k$ with $k \ge 0$ and $u_1, \dots, u_k \in L$.
nodes.title: Recognizable languages are closed under Kleene star

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ and $\tau$ be alphabets with primitive recursive encodings, let $f : \sigma \to \tau$ be primitive recursive, and let $L$ be a language over $\sigma$. If membership in $L$ is recognizable by a multi-stack machine, then so is membership in the image language $f(L) = \{f(a_1) \cdots f(a_n) : a_1 \cdots a_n \in L\}$, obtained by applying $f$ letter by letter to the words of $L$.
nodes.title: Recognizable languages are closed under alphabet maps

nodes.summary: For languages $L_1$ and $L_2$ over an alphabet $\sigma$ and a word $w$ over $\sigma$, $w$ lies in the concatenation $L_1 L_2$ if and only if there are words $u$ and $v$ with $w = uv$, $u \in L_1$ and $v \in L_2$.
nodes.title: Membership in a concatenation of languages

nodes.summary: Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be languages over an alphabet $\sigma$ with a primitive recursive encoding. If membership in $L_1$ and membership in $L_2$ are recognizable by multi-stack machines, then so is membership in the concatenation $L_1 L_2$, the set of words $uv$ with $u \in L_1$ and $v \in L_2$.
nodes.title: Recognizable languages are closed under concatenation

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be an alphabet with a primitive recursive encoding. If $L_1$ and $L_2$ are languages over $\sigma$ whose membership predicates are decidable by a multi-stack Turing machine, then the membership predicate of their concatenation $L_1 L_2 = \{uv : u \in L_1, v \in L_2\}$ is also decidable by a multi-stack Turing machine.
nodes.title: Decidable languages are closed under concatenation

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a primcodable type (it has an encoding $\mathrm{encode} : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ whose decoding is primitive recursive). If a predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ is decidable by a multi-stack machine, then so is its complement $\neg p$.
nodes.title: Decidability by multi-stack machines is closed under complement

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a primitive recursive encoding into $\mathbb{N}$. If $p$ and $q$ are recursively enumerable predicates on $\alpha$, then the predicate $a \mapsto p(a) \lor q(a)$ is recursively enumerable.
nodes.title: Recursively enumerable predicates are closed under disjunction

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a primitive recursive encoding. If $p$ and $q$ are predicates on $\alpha$ that are decidable by a multi-stack Turing machine, then so is the predicate $a \mapsto p(a) \lor q(a)$.
nodes.title: Decidable predicates are closed under disjunction

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a primitive recursive encoding. If $p$ and $q$ are predicates on $\alpha$ that are recognizable by a multi-stack Turing machine, then so is the predicate $a \mapsto p(a) \lor q(a)$.
nodes.title: Recognizable predicates are closed under disjunction

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a primitive recursive encoding into $\mathbb{N}$. If $p$ and $q$ are computable predicates on $\alpha$, then the predicate $a \mapsto p(a) \lor q(a)$ is computable.
nodes.title: Computable predicates are closed under disjunction

nodes.summary: For a word $w$ over $\sigma$, this is the list of all ways to write $w$ as a concatenation $w = u_1 u_2 \cdots u_k$ of nonempty words $u_1, \dots, u_k$, each recorded as the list $[u_1, \dots, u_k]$. The empty word has exactly one such partition, the empty list.
nodes.title: Partitions of a word into nonempty factors

nodes.summary: Given Boolean tests $f$ and $g$ on words over $\sigma$, a word $w$ and a natural number $n$, the split test is the Boolean value that is true exactly when there is some $i < n$ such that $f$ is true on the prefix of $w$ of length $\min(i, |w|)$ and $g$ is true on the remaining suffix of $w$.
nodes.title: Bounded split test

nodes.summary: For a word $w$ over $\sigma$ of length $n$, this is the list of the $n + 1$ pairs $(u, v)$ of words with $uv = w$, ordered by the length of $u$: for each $i = 0, 1, \dots, n$ it contains the prefix of $w$ of length $i$ paired with the remaining suffix.
nodes.title: Splits of a word

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a primcodable type (it has an encoding $\mathrm{encode} : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ whose decoding is primitive recursive). If a predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ is decidable by a multi-stack machine, then $p$ is co-recognizable by a multi-stack machine, that is, its complement $\neg p$ is recognizable by a multi-stack machine.
nodes.title: Decidable predicates are co-recognizable by multi-stack machines

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a primcodable type (it has an encoding $\mathrm{encode} : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ whose decoding is primitive recursive). A predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ is co-recognizable by a multi-stack machine if and only if its complement $\neg p$ is recursively enumerable, that is, the partial function on $\alpha$ that is defined, with a trivial value, exactly where $\neg p$ holds is partial recursive.
nodes.title: Multi-stack co-recognizable predicates are exactly the co-r.e. predicates

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a primcodable type (it has an encoding $\mathrm{encode} : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ whose decoding is primitive recursive). A predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ is co-recognizable by a multi-stack machine when its complement $\neg p$ is recognizable by a multi-stack machine.
nodes.title: Co-recognizability by multi-stack machines

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a primcodable type (it has an encoding $\mathrm{encode} : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ whose decoding is primitive recursive). A predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ is decidable by a multi-stack machine if and only if it is computable, that is, $p$ is decidable and its Boolean characteristic function $\alpha \to \mathrm{Bool}$ is computable.
nodes.title: Multi-stack decidable predicates are exactly the computable predicates

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a primcodable type (it has an encoding $\mathrm{encode} : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ whose decoding is primitive recursive). A predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ is decidable by a multi-stack machine if and only if it is both recognizable and co-recognizable by a multi-stack machine.
nodes.title: Post's theorem for multi-stack machines

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a primcodable type (it has an encoding $\mathrm{encode} : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ whose decoding is primitive recursive). A predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ is decidable by a multi-stack machine when there is a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ computed by a multi-stack Turing machine, with input and output numbers written in binary, such that for every $a \in \alpha$, $f(\mathrm{encode}(a)) = 1$ if…
nodes.title: Decidability by multi-stack machines

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a primcodable type (it has an encoding $\mathrm{encode} : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ whose decoding is primitive recursive). If a predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ is decidable by a multi-stack machine, then $p$ is recognizable by a multi-stack machine.
nodes.title: Decidable predicates are recognizable by multi-stack machines

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a primcodable type (it has an encoding $\mathrm{encode} : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ whose decoding is primitive recursive). A predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ is recognizable by a multi-stack machine if and only if it is recursively enumerable, that is, the partial function on $\alpha$ that is defined, with a trivial value, exactly where $p$ holds is partial recursive.
nodes.title: Multi-stack recognizable predicates are exactly the r.e. predicates

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a primcodable type (it has an encoding $\mathrm{encode} : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ whose decoding is primitive recursive). A predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ is recognizable by a multi-stack machine when there are a multi-stack Turing machine $M$ and an identification of its input alphabet with the Booleans such that for every $a \in \alpha$, $p(a)$ holds if and only if $M$ halts when started on the binary…
nodes.title: Recognizability by multi-stack machines
Theory of Computation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
